- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., after 68.27 → 69.51, model jumps to 69.34+).
- Underestimates in late horizon (last 5–10 days), particularly when true values rise sharply (e.g., 68.27 → 71.98, model fails to capture the surge).
- Shows mean reversion bias: forecasts tend to revert to prior 30-day average, but misses actual volatility or trend continuation.
- Lagged response: model reacts too slowly to recent price drops or spikes; often takes 2–3 days to adjust.
- Overconfident in short-term momentum; fails to account for policy or market correction events (e.g., EU ETS auction surprises).
- When history shows strong upward trend, model over-anticipates and over-forecasts; when downward, under-anticipates and under-forecasts.
- Avoids extreme outliers in history; tends to smooth out sharp moves, leading to underestimation of volatility or sudden reversals.
